items.titleOriginal: condense-json 1.0
items.summaryOriginal: Release: condense-json 1.0 I'm trying to get braver at releasing 1.0 versions. This little library is a year and a half old now - I've applied some sensible and non-disruptive fixes and shipped the big 1.0 for it. Here's an example of what it can do, lifted from the README: { "foo" : { "bar" : { "string" : " This is a string with foxes in it " , "nested" : { "more" : [ " Here is a string " , " another with foxes in it too " ] } } } } Combine that with a replacements object: { "1" : " with foxes in it " } And condense_json(input_json, replacements) produces the following: { "foo" : { "bar" : { "string" : { "$r" : [ " This is a string " , { "$" : " 1 " }]}, "nested" : { "more" : [ " Here is a string " , { "$r" : [ " another " , { "$" : " 1 " }, " too " ]}] } } } } It scans for strings or substrings that are present in that replacements object and replaces those with a special {"$r": ...} syntax in the output. You can reverse the effect with uncondense_json(condensed, replacements) . The idea is to make it easier to store JSON that includes duplicated data from other related structures. I use it to save space in the SQLite logs generated by LLM - see PR #1586 for the latest iteration

items.titleOriginal: OpenAI 新模型 Astra 数学表现出色，但被过度吹捧
items.summaryOriginal: OpenAI 内部测试的新模型 Astra 在数学问题上表现惊艳，但 Gary Marcus 指出相关讨论犯了"合成谬误"：擅长某类数学不等于擅长所有数学、科学乃至一切认知任务。数学之所以成为突破口，是因为它便于用符号工具验证且能廉价生成海量合成数据，而开放世界问题无法如此模拟。此外，OpenAI 未公布方法细节，尚无法评估其真实意义。

items.titleZh: OpenAI 新模型 Astra 数学表现出色，但被过度吹捧
items.titleEn: OpenAI's New Model Astra Excels at Math but Is Overhyped
items.summaryZh: OpenAI 内部测试的新模型 Astra 在数学问题上表现惊艳，但 Gary Marcus 指出相关讨论犯了"合成谬误"：擅长某类数学不等于擅长所有数学、科学乃至一切认知任务。数学之所以成为突破口，是因为它便于用符号工具验证且能廉价生成海量合成数据，而开放世界问题无法如此模拟。此外，OpenAI 未公布方法细节，尚无法评估其真实意义。
items.summaryEn: OpenAI's internally tested new model Astra shows impressive performance on math problems, but Gary Marcus points out that the discussion commits the 'composition fallacy': being good at certain types of math does not mean being good at all math, science, or all cognitive tasks. Math is a breakthrough because it is easy to verify with symbolic tools and can generate massive synthetic data cheaply, while open-world problems cannot be simulated this way. Moreover, OpenAI has not disclosed method details, so its true significance cannot be assessed.

items.titleOriginal: Meta AI uses a second AI agent as a memory coach to keep long tasks on track
items.summaryOriginal: Meta AI wants to stop AI agents from forgetting errors they've already diagnosed and repeating failed steps during complex tasks. The system improved scores by up to 8.3 percentage points across two benchmarks. items.titleOriginal: AI finds plenty of security flaws, but almost none of them get exploited
items.summaryOriginal: VulnCheck counted how often security flaws found by AI actually get exploited. Out of 1,061 AI-discovered vulnerabilities in the first half of 2026, just 14 saw confirmed attacks. That's 1.3 percent, the same rate as vulnerabilities overall. But exploits are landing faster, with the median dropping from 120 days to 80. The article AI finds plenty of security flaws, but almost none of them get exploited appeared first on The Decoder .

items.titleOriginal: Open letters about AI development
items.summaryOriginal: Open letters about AI development I wrote this summary of the past few weeks of open letters as a section of my sponsors-only newsletter but I've decided to share it here as well. Open Weights and American AI Leadership was shepherded by Microsoft, dated July 24th, and signed by 235 AI-adjacent companies including NVIDIA (see Jensen's first ever tweet ), Amazon, Y Combinator, The Linux Foundation, and (a later signer) OpenAI. It's clearly an argument designed to counter any instincts by the current US government to ban or limit open weight models over "safety" concerns - a reasonable consideration given what happened to Claude Fable 5 ! Relying solely on closed models is not inherently safe: they can be breached, misused, or fail in ways that outsiders cannot detect. And concentrating advanced AI capabilities behind a small number of closed models compounds that risk. It results in a small number of single points of failure, weakens competition, and leaves critical technology in the hands of a few providers. Open weight models, on the other hand, allow a broad community of researchers and developers to examine their behavior, identify vulnerabilities, develop safeguards, and improv

items.importanceReasonEn: The article offers timely commentary on AI policy debates, citing specific open letters and signatories, but is opinion-based without empirical data.
items.titleZh: 关于AI发展的公开信
items.titleEn: Open letters about AI development
items.summaryZh: Simon Willison 在新闻通讯中总结了最近几周的公开信。其中一封由微软主导、235家AI相关公司签署的公开信《开放权重与美国AI领导力》主张开放权重模型，反对因安全担忧而限制开源。信中指出，仅依赖封闭模型并不安全，因为封闭模型可能被攻破、滥用或存在外部无法检测的缺陷，且集中化会带来单点故障、削弱竞争。开放权重模型则能让更广泛的社区检查行为、识别漏洞并制定防护措施。
items.summaryEn: Simon Willison summarizes recent open letters in his newsletter. One letter, 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership', led by Microsoft and signed by 235 AI-related companies, argues for open-weight models against safety-based restrictions. It states that relying solely on closed models is not inherently safe, as they can be breached, misused, or fail in undetectable ways, and concentration creates single points of failure and weakens competition. Open-weight models allow a broad community to examine behavior, identify vulnerabilities, and develop safeguards.

items.summaryZh: OpenAI总裁格雷格·布罗克曼指出，在OpenAI内部，许多员工将ChatGPT接入Slack，但同事们并不喜欢被AI直接请求帮助，即使他们愿意帮助同事本人。这反映了人们重视人际关系和互助，希望AI能节省时间或增强人际互动，而不是成为人与人之间的隔阂。
items.summaryEn: Greg Brockman, President of OpenAI, notes that many employees at OpenAI connect ChatGPT to Slack, but coworkers dislike being asked for help by AI directly, even if they would be happy to help the human colleague. This reflects that people value human relationships and mutual assistance, and want AI to save time or enhance human interaction, not become a barrier between people.

items.titleOriginal: datasette-apps 0.2a0
items.summaryOriginal: Release: datasette-apps 0.2a0 Changes that improve Datasette Apps when created and edited using Datasette Agent : New app_debug() tool allowing agent to open an app (invisibly) and test it using JavaScript. #33 New app_list() tool for listing apps the user has permission to edit, so the agent can edit them. #36 The app_debug() tool is pretty neat: it works by displaying the app in a opacity: 0 iframe with pointer-events: none (so it can't be seen or interacted with) and then executing agent-provided JavaScript inside that sandboxed iframe. This means the agent can smoke test that the app is working and even do things like measure the dimensions of different elements. This uses the new context.browser_task() mechanism added in datasette-agent 0.4a0 . Tags: iframes , datasette , datasette-apps

items.titleOriginal: Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science
items.summaryOriginal: Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science A few days ago it was Anthropic discovering cryptographic weaknesses with Claude using Mythos Preview, spending $100,000 on tokens and with prompts that included "again we are not looking for low hanging fruit, we want proper research to find genuinly hard findings." Now it's OpenAI's turn to flex. They set "an internal version of Astra, our next major model" on finding solutions to ten mathematical problems that "have seen no progress on the main result for at least a decade". They claim to have spent less than $2,000 at GPT-5.6 Sol token prices on each one. (No news on how many problems they spent $2,000 on without reaching a solution though.) The openai/ten-proofs repository has Lean 4 formalizations of their results, and there's also a paper describing the solutions and an additional LLM-generated PDF where the model "reconstructs how the proof came together" based on the unpublished reasoning traces. That's a decent level of transparency, but I want to see the prompts they used! A lot of mathematicians online are experiencing a collective burst of Deep Blue . items.titleOriginal: AI keeps cracking unsolved math problems, and mathematicians have mixed feelings
items.summaryOriginal: OpenAI's refutation of the Unit Distance Conjecture has sparked a wave of AI-assisted advances in mathematics. Fields Medal winner Timothy Gowers says GPT 5.6 Pro solved two problems he had spent considerable time working on, each on its first attempt. He warns of the "possible destruction of mathematical culture" if mathematicians stop building the expertise needed to understand such results. Others simply see AI as a productivity tool. The article AI keeps cracking unsolved math problems, and mathematicians have mixed feelings appeared first on The Decoder .
items.author: Matthias Bastian
items.importanceReasonZh: 该报道涉及AI在数学领域的重大突破，以及顶尖数学家对AI影响的担忧，具有较高的行业影响力和讨论价值。
items.importanceReasonEn: The report covers significant AI breakthroughs in mathematics and top mathematicians' concerns about AI's impact, which has high industry influence and discussion value.

items.titleOriginal: AI coding agents can modernize research software but can't judge if the science is right
items.summaryOriginal: A field report from OpenAI and academic partners shows coding agents can modernize neglected research software, with speedups of up to 60x. But the systems are "eloquent, convincing, and confidently wrong in ways that are easy to miss," participants say. The effort shifts from writing code to the time-consuming work of verifying scientific correctness. The article AI coding agents can modernize research software but can't judge if the science is right appeared first on The Decoder .

items.importanceReasonZh: 该报道基于OpenAI与学术机构的实地报告，提供了编码代理在科研软件现代化中的实际应用案例，并指出了其局限性，对理解AI在科研领域的应用具有参考价值。

items.titleOriginal: A security researcher built a self-spreading worm that hides inside Word docs and hijacks Microsoft Copilot
items.summaryOriginal: A security researcher has demonstrated a worm-like attack on Microsoft Copilot for Word: invisible prompt injections hidden in documents spread automatically into new files every time they're reused. Microsoft confirmed the issue but failed to fix it after 144 days and two attempts. The article A security researcher built a self-spreading worm that hides inside Word docs and hijacks Microsoft Copilot appeared first on The Decoder .
items.author: Thomas Joos
items.importanceReasonZh: 该事件揭示了AI助手在办公软件中的安全漏洞，且微软未能及时修复，对企业和个人用户构成潜在威胁，具有较高的新闻价值和实际影响。
items.importanceReasonEn: This incident reveals security vulnerabilities in AI assistants within office software, and Microsoft's failure to promptly fix it poses potential threats to enterprises and individual users, carrying high news value and practical impact.
items.titleZh: 安全研究员构建了隐藏在Word文档中并劫持微软Copilot的自传播蠕虫
items.titleEn: A security researcher built a self-spreading worm that hides inside Word docs and hijacks Microsoft Copilot
items.summaryZh: 一位安全研究员演示了一种针对微软Copilot for Word的蠕虫式攻击：隐藏在文档中的不可见提示注入在每次文件被重用时自动传播到新文件中。微软确认了该问题，但在144天和两次尝试后未能修复。
